messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] hosted-runtime kvcache node pool: OOM spike detected on shard rtx-12 (kv_heap growth) — auto-scaling failed to reclaim. severity=sev2
alex: I'm on it. seeing sustained KV size growth tied to a few long user sessions — looks like continuous-batching + aggressive prefetch amplified contexts.
maria: can you paste the top offending keys/logs? runbook says enable eviction and throttle prefetch_depth first.
samir: attaching quick grep of logs:
```
2024-05-18T14:12:02Z runtime WARN kv_cache: insert(key=usr:SKx9..., size=24MB) ttl=0
2024-05-18T14:12:05Z runtime WARN prefetch: session=abcd ctx_len=112k tokens prefetch_depth=40
2024-05-18T14:12:07Z runtime ERROR memory: allocate failed requested=512MB avail=120MB
```
lea: customer-impact? which tenants hit errors?
nate: CS reports two paying customers had 500s on generation calls ~14:12-14:20. one is paying enterprise with SLA.
alex: severity->sev1 for customer impact + host OOMs. paging oncall now. @opsbot escalate to sme-team (runtime) and infra.
opsbot: Paging oncall rotation: alex (primary), maria (secondary). Pagerduty alert created PD-6421. :rotating_light:
maria: quick mitigation: reduce continuous_batch.window_ms to 25 and set kv.prefetch_depth=2 for hosted runtime pools. that will reduce batching aggregation and prefetch amplification.
samir: I can roll a config hotpatch via admin API. command: `curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/configs/hotpatch -d '{"pool":"hosted-rtx","continuous_batch.window_ms":25,"kv.prefetch_depth":2}'`
alex: do it but first run a dry-check to avoid thrashing latency. apply to one AZ/pool as canary.
samir: applying canary now to pool hosted-rtx-eu-west-1a...
opsbot: deploy started: canary hosted-rtx-eu-west-1a -> job 9876
alex: monitoring metrics: kv_heap_bytes down on canary, tail latency up slightly (p95 +30ms) but within SLO. good.
lea: notify affected customer with ETA. nate, please draft a quick note: we mitigated OOMs, temporary perf tradeoff while we patch.
nate: drafting: "We're aware of errors 14:12-14:20 caused by unusually long prompts triggering cache growth. We've applied a temporary config to throttle prefetching and batching to stop host OOMs. You may see small p95 latency increases. Working on a safer long-term fix."
maria: next step: enable eviction policy 'session-tail-trim' on the problematic pools to reclaim stale session prefixes. command below:
```
# enable tail-trim eviction
kubectl exec -n runtime mgr-ctl -- /usr/bin/runtimectl evict --policy=session-tail-trim --target-pool=hosted-rtx
```
samir: running eviction now against canary pool. will wait 60s for stabilization.
alex: also disable aggressive prefetch for endpoints with ctx_length > 64k. add rule to routing: `if ctx_tokens > 64000 -> prefetch_depth=1`
maria: posted that rule to ops-config repo, PR 412 — will merge on green.
opsbot: canary stable. KHeap reduced from 88%->45% in 3m.
alex: rolling hotpatch to remaining AZs (eu-west-1b, us-west-2a) with staged pause 30s between AZs.
samir: roll started. job 9877, 9878.
lea: action item: product to add quota/guard for extremely long single prompts to avoid cache blowups. @samir can you estimate ETA?
samir: I can prototype a guard in 24-48h, but we should add an emergency rule this week to reject >200k token requests with a 4xx and guidance.
alex: agreed. create internal task and link to incident.
opsbot: incident timeline created: INC-20240518-2142.
nate: customer update sent. initial replies positive, asked for RCA.
maria: retrospective notes: root cause = combination of long user sessions, continuous-batching aggregation window too large, and prefetch depth not gated by ctx length. fix path: hotpatch (done), eviction policy (done), routing guard (in progress), longer-term patch: smarter batching heuristic + KV compression.
alex: closing loop: monitoring for next 2h, if stable we'll downgrade to sev2 and then close after RCA and postmortem. great job team. :tada:
